issues.description: The template file template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named AnimalFarm inside a file called Farm.java and contains duplicated/embedded package and class declarations (e.g. a 'package' statement inside a method and a duplicated class block). The problem statement and solution expect a public class named Farm with the specified methods and attributes. The file-name/class-name mismatch and the syntactic duplication will cause compilation errors and prevent students from implementing or testing the intended Farm class, blocking progress.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the contents of template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a proper public class named Farm (matching the file name) that declares the List<Animal> animals attribute and the required method stubs (addAnimal, singFarmSong, singFarmSongVerse, feedAllAnimals, getters/setters). Remove the duplicated package statement and any embedded/duplicate class blocks so the template compiles and matches the problem UML/solution structure.

issues.description: The template repository defines a class named 'AnimalFarm' inside Farm.java, while the problem statement and the solution use the class name 'Farm'. This inconsistent identifier (AnimalFarm vs Farm) for the same conceptual entity (the farm container class) creates direct mapping confusion: students will look for a 'Farm' class as required by the exercise and UML, but the template provides 'AnimalFarm', preventing straightforward mapping from requirements to the starter code and final solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (or change file name to match class), so the class name matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the public class name equals the file name (Farm) to avoid student confusion.
